events.title: Taiwan Bourse May Take Further Damage On Friday
events.description: The Taiwan stock market headed south again on Thursday, one day after ending the two-day losing streak in which it had given up almost 820 points or 1.7 percent. The Taiwan Stock Exchange now sits just above the 46,040-point plateau and it figures to see continued consolidation on Friday.

events.title: Singapore Stock Market May Give Up Support At 5,400 Points
events.description: The Singapore stock market turned lower again on Thursday, one day after ending the two-day losing streak in which it had dipped more than 10 points or 0.2 percent. The STI now sits just above the 5,415-point plateau and it's likely to open under water again on Friday.

events.title: Japan Inflation Climbs 2.1% On Year In September
events.description: Overall consumer prices in Japan were up 2.1 percent on year in September, the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications said on Friday - in line with expectations and up from 1.9 percent in August.

events.title: Rally May Stall For Malaysia Stock Market
events.description: The Malaysia stock market has finished higher in three straight sessions, collecting more than 10 points or 0.6 percent in that span. The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index now sits just beneath the 1,610-point plateau although it may run out of steam on Friday.

events.title: Japan Stock Market May Extend Thursday's Losses
events.description: The Japan stock market headed south again on Thursday, one day after ending the two-day slide in which it had tumbled almost 1,300 points or 2 percent. The Nikkei now sits just above the 62,900-point plateau and it may take further damage again on Friday.

events.title: Tech Shares Likely To Weigh On South Korea Shares
events.description: The South Korea stock market has finished lower in two of three trading days since the end of the two-day winning streak in which it had rallied more than 210 points or 3.6 percent. The KOSPI now sits just above the 5,740-point plateau and it may extend its losses on Friday.

events.title: Australia Manufacturing PMI Improves To 49.7 - S&P Global
events.description: The manufacturing sector in Australia continued to contract in October, albeit at a slightly slower pace, the latest survey from S&P Global revealed on Friday with a manufacturing PMI score of 49.7.

events.title: Japan Inflation Data Due On Friday
events.description: Japan will on Friday release September figures for consumer prices, highlighting a modest day for Asia-Pacific economic activity. In August, overall inflation was up 0.1 percent on month and 1.9 percent on year, while core CPI rose an annual 1.7 percent.

events.title: U.S. Dollar Slips As Bets On Federal Reserve Rate Hike Decline
events.description: The U.S. Dollar value turned lower on Thursday amid reversal in the U.S. Federal Reserve's rate hike expectations from yesterday's 14% to nearly 7%. The shift overshadowed the safe-haven demand tied to concerns over high inflation that surfaced after New York Times reported possible fresh attacks on Iran by the U.S. in November.

events.title: Swiss Market Ends Roughly Flat
events.description: The Switzerland stock market's benchmark index SMI ended slightly down on Thursday after languishing in negative territory for almost the entire trading session. Investors mostly made their moves, reacting to corporate earnings updates.

events.title: European Equities Fall On Multiple Headwinds Including Oil Spike
events.description: European equities fell Thursday as investors worried about AI infrastructure spending, Middle East tensions, and elevated oil prices. The Stoxx 600 declined 1.05%, with mining and bank stocks leading losses. Brent crude surged 3.5% above $112.50 per barrel.

events.title: Tech, Commodity Stocks Weakness Hurts Canadian Market
events.description:
The Canadian market is down sharply in negative territory a little past noon on Thursday, weighed down by sharp losses in energy, materials and technology sectors. 

Rising concerns about inflation and possible rate hikes by the Federal Reserve and the Bank of Canada this year, and worries about AI spending contributed to market's decline.

events.title: Eurozone Consumer Confidence Sinks To 5-Month Low Amid Widespread Unrest Against Inflation
events.description: Euro area consumer sentiment eroded at a faster-than-expected pace in October to reach its lowest level in five months as several countries witness public unrest against a host of issues from the rising cost of living to poor education infrastructure.
